_comment: One unit of competency. It exists as a file because the catalogue lists a unit — and Moodle gets a grade item for it — only once this file ships. The lessons below were READ OFF the built pages' data-criteria, not asserted here, so this cannot drift from what is actually taught.
title: The computers you already use
framework: Professor Adow TVET — Digital Skills for the Workshop

criteria.text: Name the four things every computer does — take input, process it, store it, give output — and point to each one on a device used in your own trade.
Identify the computer inside a piece of equipment that is not called a computer: a moisture meter, a welding inverter, a vehicle diagnostic tool, a milk chiller, a feed scale.
criteria.evidence: Identification task from photographs or real equipment.

criteria.text: Distinguish a general-purpose computer from an embedded one, and explain why a machine's controller cannot simply be used for something else.
Separate a mechanical fault from a digital one on the same machine, and say which trade attends to each.
State what data a workplace device holds, who it belongs to, and what may not be copied or removed from it.
Start up, log in to and shut down a shared workshop computer without losing another person's work.
Report a device fault so a technician can act on it: what was being done, what happened, what was expected instead.
criteria.evidence: Written fault report assessed against a rubric.
